subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Group B: The Killer Era
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Group B: The Killer Era.

hook.text: In the 1980s, Group B rally cars were so fast and so dangerous that the FIA had to ban them.

buildup.text: Manufacturers built mid-engine monsters with turbochargers producing over 500 horsepower on dirt roads.

discovery.text: The Audi Quattro used all-wheel drive to put that power down, changing rally technology forever.

twist.text: Fans stood inches from the track as cars flew past at 120 mph—and multiple spectators were killed.

climax.text: After fatal crashes in 1986 killed drivers and fans, the FIA banned Group B and slowed rally cars down.

punchline.text: The most exciting rally era was too dangerous to survive.

quiz.question: Why was Group B rally racing banned?
options: Multiple fatal crashes of drivers and spectators
Teams were cheating on engine rules

details.summary: Group B rally was a brief but legendary era from 1982 to 1986 where minimal regulations allowed cars with over 500 horsepower to race on narrow roads inches from spectators, with fatal consequences.
details.whyItMatters: Group B produced the most extreme rally cars ever built but was banned after fatal crashes. Its legacy warns that pushing performance without safety limits has devastating consequences.
takeaways: Minimal regulations allowed up to 600 HP in lightweight cars
Spectators stood on roads, creating lethal conditions
Fatal crashes in 1986 prompted an immediate ban on the class

faq.question: What made Group B cars so special?
faq.answer: Manufacturers only had to build 200 road cars to homologate their race cars, allowing extreme lightweight construction and enormous turbocharged power. The resulting machines were more prototype than production vehicle.

faq.question: Why was Group B banned?
faq.answer: After multiple fatal crashes, including the deaths of Henri Toivonen and his co-driver in Corsica in 1986, the FIA immediately cancelled Group B. The cars were simply too fast for the roads and crowd conditions.
